questions.text: Which of the following statements is true according to the passage?

options.text: The child from Tikrikilla was conclusively diagnosed with wild poliovirus.
The switch from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine in India occurred in 2015.
WPV type 2 was globally eradicated in 2016.
The last WPV type 3 case was reported globally in 2019.
Pakistan has reported zero WPV type 1 cases in 2024.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Statement 1: The child from Tikrikilla was conclusively diagnosed with wild poliovirus.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage states there is no official report confirming whether it is caused by wild poliovirus or vaccine-derived poliovirus.
  • Statement 2: The switch from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine in India occurred in 2015.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage mentions that the switch happened in 2016, not 2015.
  • Statement 3: WPV type 2 was globally eradicated in 2016.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage states that WPV type 2 was eradicated in 2015.
  • Statement 4: The last WPV type 3 case was reported globally in 2019.
    • This statement is correct as the passage confirms, "the global eradication of the wild poliovirus (WPV) type 2 in 2015 and the WPV type 3 in 2019."
  • Statement 5: Pakistan has reported zero WPV type 1 cases in 2024.

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following statements about the oral polio vaccine (OPV) in India is false?

The switch to IPV has been recommended but not executed in India.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.

  • India switched from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine (OPV) in 2016.
  • The bivalent OPV contains live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 viruses, not type 2 virus.
  • The passage mentions that it's impossible for the child to have the type 2 virus from the oral vaccine given in India because India made the switch to the bivalent vaccine, which does not include type 2 virus.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Information: "India made the globally significant switch in 2016 from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine that has only live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 virus."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1) India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in 2016 – True: The passage confirms this switch.
  • Option 2) Bivalent OPV contains live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 viruses – True: The bivalent OPV includes these specific types.
  • Option 4) Immunodeficient children should not receive OPV – True: The passage explicitly mentions this recommendation.
  • Option 5) The switch to IPV has been recommended but not executed in India – True: The passage suggests an urgent need for the switch to IPV, which has not been fully implemented.

  • Only B: Incorrect because B cannot be inferred from the passage.
  • All A, B, and C: Incorrect because B cannot be inferred from the passage.
  • Only C: Incorrect because both A and C can be inferred from the passage.

questions.text:
Given Below is a sentence with two blanks. Identify the correct order of words which can be used to fill in the blanks.

The menu at Sam’s Riverside is _______ by seasonality, so very little is now _______ in Europe.

A. Dictated
B. Portrait 
C. Spurned
D. Refused
E. Sourced
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is AE.

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the given words:
    • Dictated - controlled or decisively affected; determined.
    • Portrait - denoting a format of printed matter which is higher than it is wide.
    • Spurned - rejected with disdain or contempt.
    • Refused - indicated or showed that one is not willing to do something.
    • Sourced - found out where (something) can be obtained.

Important Points

  • In the sentence, the menu at Sam's depends on seasons—items will only be available for a certain season. So, 'Dictated' is the correct word for the first blank. 
  • Since the menu is seasonal we get the hint that they are not getting much from Europe because of the current season. So, 'Sourced' must be the correct word for the second blank. 
  • From the meanings given, the words 'Dictated' and 'Sourced' are grammatically and conceptually correct.​​


So the correct sentence is - The menu at Sam’s Riverside is dictated by seasonality, so very little is now sourced in Europe.

So the correct sentence is - The environment and urban planning minister, Murat Kurum said people were trapped under the wreckage and rescue efforts were underway.

questions.text:
Select the phrase/connector from the given three options which can be used to form a single sentence from the two sentences given below, implying the same as expressed in the statement sentences.

Sharma was a contemporary of such political stalwarts as Arun Jaitley, Abhishek Singhvi and Vijay Goel. He was a rising political star when he cut his own career short by killing his wife in 1995.

1. After being a contemporary of

2. Being a contemporary of such political

3. Since he was a rising political star
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Only 2.
Key Points

  • The phrase that can connect both the given sentences and imply the same meaning is only 2.
    • 'Being' is used with a person or thing that exists. The two statements talk about "Sharma". The first states whose contemporary he was, while the second states how he cut his political career by killing his wife. Clearly, the above synthesis is both grammatically and contextually correct.
  • 'After being a contemporary': at a later or future time; afterwards. The second statement is not a consequence of the first one. Hence, this option is ruled out.
  • ​'Since': from a particular time in the past until a later time, or until now. The two statements do not show a cause and effect relationship, thus, since, can be eliminated.


The sentence after using the phrase is-

  • Being a contemporary of such political stalwarts as Arun Jaitley, Abhishek Singhvi and Vijay Goel, Sharma, was a rising political star who cut his own career short by killing his wife in 1995.

Additional Information

Let us understand the meanings of some important words:

  • Contemporary: belonging to the same or a stated period in the past
  • Stalwarts: a loyal, reliable, and hard-working supporter of or participant in an organization

questions.text:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Every student in the  (a) / class contribute actively during (b)  / discussions, fostering a collaborative learning environment. (c) / More than one of the above (d) / None of the above (e)
questions.explanation:
The erroneous part is 'b'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in Part: "class contribute actively during."
  • The correct form should be "contributes actively during" instead of "contribute actively during."
  • The subject-verb agreement is incorrect in this sentence. When using "every," it indicates singular and requires a singular verb form to match.
  • In this case, "Every student" is the subject, and "student" is singular. Therefore, the verb should also be singular to agree with the subject.
  • Example: 
    • Correct: Every student in the class contributes actively during discussions.
    • Incorrect: Every student in the class contribute actively during discussions.
  • The corrected sentence maintains proper subject-verb agreement by using the singular verb "contributes" to match the singular subject "Every student." 
     

Correct Sentence: Every student in the class contributes actively during discussions, fostering a collaborative learning environment.

questions.text:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The book, along with  (a) / its accompanying illustrations (b) /, provide a comprehensive understanding of the historical era. (c) / More than one of the above (d) / None of the above (e)
questions.explanation:
The erroneous part is 'c'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in Part]: "provide a comprehensive understanding of the historical era."
  • The correct form should be "provides a comprehensive" instead of "provide a comprehensive."
  • When a sentence includes a subject along with a phrase such as "along with," "as well as," or "together with," the subject-verb agreement is determined by the main subject before the phrase, not by the words within the phrase.
  • In this case, "The book" is the main subject, and "its accompanying illustrations" is a phrase providing additional information. The main subject, "The book," is singular, so the verb "provides" should also be singular to agree with the subject.
  • Example:
    • Singular Subject: The book, along with its author, provides insight into historical events.
    • Incorrect Plural Verb: The book, along with its author, provide insight into historical events.
  • The corrected sentence would read: "The book, along with its accompanying illustrations, provides a comprehensive understanding of the historical era."
  • This adjustment ensures proper subject-verb agreement, where the singular subject requires a singular verb.

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.
 
Prodigiously
 
A. Carlos Alcaraz is a prodigiously talented player who has already won multiple Grand Slam titles.
B. Prodigiously nervous, the pianist played with a trembling hand throughout the concert.
C. The prodigiously massive library contains volumes from ancient to modern times.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Option 2 - Both A & C.

Key Points

  • The word "Prodigiously" means to an unusually great, remarkable, or impressive degree; enormously. (असाधारण रूप से, बहुत अधिक)
    • Example: The young athlete has improved prodigiously over the past year.
  • "Prodigiously talented" means exceptionally or extraordinarily talented, making sentence A an appropriate use of the word. (असाधारण रूप से प्रतिभाशाली)
    • Example: Carlos Alcaraz is a prodigiously talented player who has achieved remarkable success at a young age.
  • "Prodigiously massive" means extremely or extraordinarily large, making sentence C an appropriate use of the word. (असाधारण रूप से विशाल)
    • Example: The museum houses a prodigiously massive collection of historical manuscripts.
  • Sentence B is not an appropriate use of "prodigiously" because the word is generally used to emphasize an unusually great degree of size, quantity, ability, or achievement rather than a temporary emotional state such as nervousness.

Therefore, the correct answer is- Both A & C.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and examples:

  • Only A (केवल A): This option is incorrect because sentence C also uses "prodigiously" appropriately.
    • Example: Sentence A correctly describes an exceptionally talented player.
  • Only C (केवल C): This option is incorrect because sentence A also correctly conveys the meaning of "prodigiously."
    • Example: The scientist was prodigiously successful in his research.
  • All A, B & C (A, B और C सभी): This option is incorrect because sentence B uses "prodigiously nervous" in an unsuitable context.
    • Example: The phrase "prodigiously nervous" does not appropriately convey the intended meaning of the word.
  • None of these (इनमें से कोई नहीं): This option is incorrect because sentences A and C correctly use the word "prodigiously."
    • Example: The artist was prodigiously talented and produced an extraordinary body of work.

Condone

questions.explanation:

Key Points

  • Condone: to accept or allow behaviour that is morally wrong or offensive to continue. (अनदेखी करना, माफ़ करना)
  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:
  • Sentence A: The principal could not condone such rude behaviour in the school.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "condone" to describe the principal not accepting rude behavior.
  • Sentence B: We cannot condone any form of discrimination in our company.
    • This sentence also correctly uses the word "condone" to describe not accepting any form of discrimination.
  • Sentence C: She condone the delicious food at the new restaurant.
    • This sentence incorrectly uses the word "condone," as it does not fit the context of accepting or allowing morally wrong behavior.
  • So, both sentences A and B correctly use the word "condone" to illustrate not accepting certain behaviors, while sentence C does not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & B."

questions.text:

questions.explanation:

  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:

    • This sentence correctly uses the word "perpetuate" to describe the continuation of poverty due to ineffective policies.
  • Sentence B: They sought to perpetuate the charitable traditions started by their ancestors.
    • This sentence also correctly uses the word "perpetuate" to describe the continuation of charitable traditions.
  • Sentence C: The artist wanted to perpetuate his ideas into the canvas quickly.
    • This sentence does not correctly use the word "perpetuate" as it implies causing something to continue, not the act of transferring ideas quickly.
  • So, both sentences A and B correctly use the word "perpetuate" to illustrate different contexts of causing something to continue.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & B."

questions.text:
Directions: In the following question, two statements are given with some words in bold. Which of the following pairs of bold words must be interchanged to make both sentences grammatically correct?

a. School administrators were crooked(A) to find a resolution(B) to the parent's vehement(C) about her child being bullied on the bus.

b. The voters were complaint(D) in their efforts to remove(E) the eager(F) politician from office.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'FBDCEA.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'a' talks about School administrators eager to find a plan to solve the parent's complaint about her child being bullied on the bus.
  • The sentence 'b' talks about the voters showing very strong feelings, especially anger in their efforts to remove the dishonest politician from office.
  • Let us explore the meaning of the highlighted words:
    • Crooked - Not honest. (बेईमान, कपटी)
    • Resolution - Solving or settling a problem, dispute, etc. (समस्‍या, विवाद आदि का समाधान या निपटारा)
    • Vehement - Showing very strong (often negative) feelings, especially anger. (भावना, विशेषतः क्रोध की दृष्टि से प्रचंड, उग्र)
    • Complaint - A statement that you are not satisfied with something. (शिकायत, असंतोष का कारण)
    • Remove - To take somebody or something off or away. (व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु को हटा या मिटा देना)
    • Eager - Strongly wanting to do or have something. (आतुर, इच्छुक)
  • Thus, (A) and (F) must be interchanged and, (C) and (D) must be interchanged.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 5.

questions.text:

a. It's hard to remorse(A) the suffering(B) of a man who caused so much murder(C) to so many people.

b. The psychopath appeared content(D) and showed no lament(E) during the harm(F) trial.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'EBFDAC.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'a' says it's hard to express regret or disappointment about the suffering of a man who caused so much murder to so many people.
  • The sentence 'b' talks about a psychopath who appeared satisfied and showed no feeling of sadness during the murder trial.
  • Let us explore the meaning of the highlighted words:

    • Suffering - The state of undergoing pain, distress, or hardship. (पीड़ा, कष्‍ट या वेदना)

  • Thus, (A) and (E) must be interchanged and, (C) and (F) must be interchanged.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 5.

questions.text: Which of the following words is similar in meaning to "expenditure" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:

Key Points

To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word "expenditure" in the context of the passage:

    • For Example -
    • The government's expenditure on healthcare increased significantly in the last budget.

 

Now, let's consider the options:

  • Expansion - the action of becoming larger or more extensive (विस्तार)

  • Profit - the financial gain or benefit derived from a business or investment (लाभ)

  • Liability - the state of being responsible for something, especially a financial obligation or debt (देयता)

  • Outlay - an amount of money spent or allocated for a specific purpose, often as part of a budget or plan (व्यय)

After understanding the meanings of these words, we can conclude that the word "outlay" is most similar in meaning to "expenditure" in the context of the passage, as both words refer to the allocation or spending of funds or resources as part of a planned and organized financial activity.

In the question below, a statement and assumptions numbered I and II are given. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. You have to consider the following assumption and decide which of the assumption is implicit in the statement.

Statements: If the importance of educational certificates is ignored in the job sector, students will think a lot before joining a college.

Assumptions:

I) Students join college for education as well as to obtain a job.

II) There is no use of a degree to get a job.

options.text: Either I or II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation:
Given statements: If the importance of educational certificates is ignored in the job sector, students will think a lot before joining a college.

Assumptions:

I) Students join college for education as well as to obtain a job → True (The statement directly indicates that getting a job is the major reason for students to join a college).

II) There is no use of a degree to get a job → False (This assumption is unrelated to the statement).

Hence, Only assumption I is implicit.

Statement:

Psychologists say work overload leads to stress and mental disorders. But some famous personalities say that they find work an antidote to stress.

Conclusions:

I. Some famous personalities are overloaded by work.

II. Psychologists do not judge properly every time.

According to the given statement, there is no information given about the famous personalities who are not stressed. Hence, I do not follow. In the second part of the statement, the Psychologists opinion is proved wrong. Hence, we can conclude that the Psychologist's judgment is not proper.

Hence, only II follows.

Directions: A statement is given followed by two inferences I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given inferences, if any, follow from the given statement.

Statement: One way to cut effluents while earning revenues is to price the carbon content of domestic production and imports.

Inference:

I.Domestic production leads to the generation and release of carbon-related compounds into the environment.

 II.Production and release of carbon-generated compounds are undesirable.
questions.explanation:
The statement mentions that the carbon-rich discharge from domestic industry and imports can be managed effectively and brought down by charging revenue.

From what has been supplied it can be deduced that domestic production leads to the generation of carbon-related content into the environment. So, inference I follows.

Also, from the supplied statement it can be inferred that the production of carbon-related content is not environment friendly therefore there is a need to regulate its emissions. So, inference II follows.

Hence, Both I and II follow.
